newsitem.title: UK: Explosion outside U.N. building in Bosnia - BBC.
newsitem.headline: Explosion outside U.N. building in Bosnia - BBC.

text.p: An explosion has occurred outside the U.N. police headquarters in the town Zvornic in eastern Bosnia, BBC radio reported on Monday.
Few details were available but the Bosnian Serb news agency reported that a vehicle was blown up in the blast, the BBC said.

The explosion occurred a few hours after Bosnian Serb leaders honoured a notorious police chief as a fallen hero on Sunday, three days after British soldiers shot him dead when he resisted arrest on war crimes charges.
Simo Drljaca, a former police chief of Prijedor who led ethnic cleansing against Moslems and Croats in 1992, was killed after he opened fire on British special forces.

While Bosnian Serbs portrayed Drljaca's death as murder, British Defence Secretary George Robertson said the attempt to arrest him signalled a crackdown on suspects wanted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal for former Yugoslavia.
"This (incident) will have upset a lot of people who thought they were getting away with it," he said.

Another Serb, Milan Kovacevic, was seized by British troops, also on Thursday, and extradited to The Hague as part of "Operation Tango". The NATO raid broke new ground for the alliance, which had previously ruled out going after suspects unless peacekeeping troops happened to stumble upon them.
